source_text: Ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῦ λόγου διπλῆ τίς ἐστιν ἔννοια. Ὁ μὲν γάρ τίς ἐστιν ὁ διὰ τῆς φωνῆς προφερόμενος, οὗτος ὁ μετὰ τὸ προενεχθῆναι τῷ ἀέρι ἐναπολλύμενος· ὁ δέ τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἐνδιάθετος, ἐνυπάρχων ἡμῶν ταῖς καρδίαις· ὁ ἐννοηματικός. Καὶ ἄλλος, ὁ τεχνικὸς λόγος. Ὅρα μή ποτέ σε παρακρούσηται τὸ ὁμώνυμον τῆς φωνῆς. Πῶς γὰρ ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ ὁ ἀνθρώπινος λόγος, τοῦ ἀνθρώ που κάτω που λαβόντος τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς γενέσεως; Πρὸ ἀνθρώπου θηρία· πρὸ ἀνθρώπου κτήνη, τὰ ἑρπετὰ πάντα· ὅσα χερσαῖα, καὶ ὅσα ἔνυδρα, πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἀστέρες, ἥλιος, σελήνη, βοτάναι, σπέρ ματα, γῆ, θάλαττα, οὐρανός. Οὐ τοίνυν ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ ἀνθρώπινος λόγος, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ὁ τῶν ἀγγέλων. Πᾶσα γὰρ ἡ κτίσις κατωτέρα τῶν αἰώνων ἐστὶ, τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ εἶναι λαβοῦσα παρὰ τοῦ κτίσαντος. Ὁ δὲ ἐν καρ δίᾳ λόγος, καὶ αὐτὸς ἑκάστου τῶν νοηθέντων ἐστὶ νεώτερος. Ἀλλ' ἄκουε τοῦ λόγου θεοπρεπῶς. Περὶ γὰρ τοῦ Μονογενοῦς διαλεγόμενός σοι, Λόγον εἶπεν αὐτόν. Ὥσπερ οὖν καὶ φῶς μετ' ὀλίγον ἐρεῖ, καὶ ζωὴν, καὶ ἀνάστασιν, καὶ οὔτε φῶς ἀκούσας, ἐπὶ τὸ αἰσθητὸν τοῦτο καὶ ὀφθαλμοῖς ὁρατὸν καταφέρῃ, οὔτε ζωὴν ἀκούσας, τὴν κοινὴν ταύτην νοεῖς, ἣν καὶ τὰ ἄλογα ζῇ· οὕτω καὶ Λόγον ἀκούων, φύλαξαι μήποτε τῇ σῇ ἀσθενείᾳ τῆς διανοίας πρὸς χαμαιζήλους καὶ ταπεινὰς διανοίας ὑπενεχθῇς. Ἀλλ' ἐρεύνα τὴν διά νοιαν τοῦ ῥήματος. Διὰ τί Λόγος; Ἵνα δειχθῇ, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ νοῦ προῆλθε. Διὰ τί Λόγος; Ὅτι ἀπαθῶς ἐγεννήθη. Διὰ τί Λόγος; Ὅτι εἰκὼν τοῦ γεννήσαντος, ὅλον ἐν ἑαυτῷ δεικνὺς τὸν γεννήσαντα, οὐδὲν ἐκεῖθεν ἀπομερίσας, καὶ τέλειος ὑπάρχων καθ' ἑαυ τόν· ὡς καὶ ὁ ἡμέτερος λόγος ὅλην ἡμῶν ἀπεικονίζει τὴν ἔννοιαν. Ἃ γὰρ κατὰ καρδίαν ἐνενοήσαμεν, ταῦτα τῷ ῥήματι προηνέγκαμεν, καὶ ἔστι τοῦ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ νοήματος ἀπεικόνισμα τὸ λαλούμενον. Ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας ὁ λόγος προφέρεται. Καὶ ἔστιν ἡ μὲν καρδία ἡμῶν οἷον πηγή τις, ὁ δὲ προφερόμενος λόγος οἷον ὁλκός τις ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς ταύτης ῥέων. Τοσοῦτον οὖν τὸ ἀποῤῥέον, ὅσον τὸ πρώτως ἀναφερόμενον· καὶ οἷον τὸ κεκρυμμένον, τοσοῦτον καὶ τὸ φαινόμενον. Λόγον οὖν εἶπεν, ἵνα τὴν ἀπαθῆ σοι γέννησιν τοῦ Πατρὸς παραστήσῃ, καὶ τὴν τελείαν ὕπαρξίν σοι τοῦ Υἱοῦ θεολογήσῃ, καὶ τὴν ἄχρονον συνάφειαν τοῦ Υἱοῦ πρὸς Πατέρα διὰ τούτων ἐνδείξηται. Καὶ γὰρ ὁ ἡμέτερος λόγος τοῦ νοῦ γέννημα, ἀπαθῶς γεννώμενος· οὔτε γὰρ τέμνε ται, οὔτε μερίζεται, οὔτε ῥέει· ἀλλὰ μένων ὅλος ὁ νοῦς ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ συστάσει, ὅλον τὸν λόγον καὶ ἀπηρτισμένον ὑφίστησι· καὶ προελθὼν ὁ λόγος, πᾶσαν τοῦ γεννήσαντος νοῦ τὴν δύναμιν ἐν ἑαυτῷ περιέχει. Ὅσον οὖν εὐσεβὲς, τοσοῦτον λαβὼν πρὸς τὴν τοῦ Μονογενοῦς θεολογίαν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ λόγου φωνῆς· ὅπερ ἂν εὕρῃς ἀπεμφαῖνον καὶ ἀνάρμοστον φαινό μενον, τοῦτο παραίτησαι, καὶ ὑπέρβηθι μηχανῇ πάσῃ. Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ Λόγος. Εἰ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ Υἱὸς, τῇ προσηγορίᾳ τοῦ Υἱοῦ συνεισῆλθεν ἄν σοι ἡ περὶ τοῦ πάθους ἔννοια.
thought_title: Why John says Word rather than Son
orientation: Basil is answering the question of what kind of “word” was in the beginning, and now explains why the Evangelist chose the name Word for the only Son.
pass_a_gloss: But also of the word there is a double meaning. For one is the word brought forth through the voice, this one after being brought forth perishing into the air; and another is the inward word, existing in our hearts; the conceptual word. And another, the technical word. See that the homonymy of the sound never deceives you. For how was the human word in the beginning, since the human somewhere below received the beginning of generation? Before the human were wild beasts; before the human were cattle, all the creeping things; as many as are land animals, and as many as are water animals, birds of heaven, stars, sun, moon, plants, seeds, earth, sea, heaven. Not therefore in the beginning was the human word, but neither the word of angels. For all creation is lower than the ages, having received the beginning of being from the creator. But the word in the heart, this too is younger than each of the things thought. But hear the word in a manner worthy of God. For speaking to you about the only Son, he called him Word. Just as therefore also light after a little he will say, and life, and resurrection, and neither hearing light do you bring it down to this perceptible and visible-to-the-eyes light, nor hearing life do you think this common life, which also the irrational animals live; so also hearing Word, guard yourself lest ever by the weakness of your understanding you be carried down to lowly and humble thoughts. But search out the meaning of the saying. Why Word? So that it might be shown, that from the mind he came forth. Why Word? Because without passion he was begotten. Why Word? Because he is image of the begetter, showing in himself the whole begetter, having divided off nothing from there, and being perfect in himself; as also our word images forth our whole thought. For what things we thought in the heart, these things we brought forth in the saying, and the thing spoken is a representation of the thought in the heart. For out of the abundance of the heart the word is brought forth. And our heart is like a certain spring, and the word brought forth is like a certain channel flowing from this spring. As much therefore is the outflowing, as much as the first rising up; and as the hidden thing is, so much also is the appearing thing. Word therefore he said, so that he might present to you the passionless generation of the Father, and might theologize for you the perfect existence of the Son, and might indicate through these things the timeless union of the Son to the Father. For also our word is offspring of the mind, begotten without passion; for it is neither cut, nor divided, nor does it flow; but the mind remaining whole in its own constitution, establishes the whole word also complete; and the word having come forth, contains in itself all the power of the begetting mind. As much therefore as is pious, so much having taken toward the theology of the only Son from the sound of the word; whatever you find incongruous and appearing unfitting, this reject, and pass over it by every device. In the beginning was the Word. But if he had said: In the beginning was the Son, with the title of Son there would have entered in with it for you the thought about passion.

choices.why: Basil contrasts the spoken word with the word that remains within the heart; 'inward' preserves the spatial metaphor of residing inside.
This is a third term Basil adds to clarify the inward word as belonging to thought; 'conceptual' keeps the link to νοῦς and thought.
Basil warns that the same spoken sound 'word' can mislead; 'homonymy' is precise for same name with different meanings.

choices.english: in a manner worthy of God
choices.why: Basil urges hearing 'Word' in a way befitting God, not human words; the rendering keeps the compound's force.
The glossary requires 'without passion' for ἀπαθής; 'was begotten' keeps the passive voice and the generation term.
ἄχρονος means without time; 'timeless' is direct and preserves the negation of time.

pass_b_english: But the word “word” carries a double meaning. One kind is the word spoken aloud, which perishes in the air as soon as it is uttered. The other is the inward word, dwelling in our hearts—the conceptual word. And there is yet another, the word of skill. Take care that the homonymy of the sound never deceives you. For how could the human word have been in the beginning, when the human being received the beginning of his generation somewhere far below? Before the human being came the wild beasts; before the human being came the cattle, all the creeping things, everything that walks on land and everything that lives in water, the birds of heaven, the stars, the sun, the moon, the plants, the seeds, the earth, the sea, the sky. So the human word was not in the beginning—and neither was the word of angels. For every creature is lower than the ages, having received the beginning of its being from the Creator. And the word in the heart is itself younger than each of the things thought. But hear the word in a manner worthy of God. For when he speaks to you about the only Son, he called him Word. Just as he will shortly say “light” and “life” and “resurrection,” and when you hear “light” you do not sink down to this light perceived by the senses and visible to the eyes, and when you hear “life” you do not think of this common life that even the irrational animals live—so too, when you hear “Word,” guard yourself lest through the weakness of your understanding you be dragged down to lowly and humble thoughts. Search out the meaning of the saying. Why “Word”? So that it might be shown that he came forth from the mind. Why “Word”? Because without passion he was begotten. Why “Word”? Because he is the image of the one who begot him, showing the whole begetter in himself, dividing off nothing from there, and existing complete in himself—just as our own word images forth our whole thought. For what we have conceived in the heart, that we bring forth in speech, and what is spoken is a representation of the thought in the heart. For out of the abundance of the heart the word is brought forth. Our heart is like a spring, and the word brought forth is like a channel flowing from that spring. What flows away is as much as what first rises up; and what is hidden is as much as what appears. He said “Word,” then, to present to you the generation of the Father without passion, to proclaim to you the complete existence of the Son, and through these things to indicate the timeless union of the Son with the Father. For our own word is the offspring of the mind, begotten without passion: it is not cut, it is not divided, it does not flow away. Rather, the mind remains whole in its own constitution and brings forth the whole word, complete and finished; and the word, having come forth, contains in itself all the power of the mind that begot it. Take from the sound of the word “word,” then, as much as is reverent for the theology of the only Son; whatever you find incongruous and appearing out of place, reject it and pass beyond it by every means. “In the beginning was the Word.” If he had said, “In the beginning was the Son,” the thought of passion would have entered with the title “Son.”

last_rejected.why: "Technical" or "artistic" word, not "skill"; refers to specialized/craft discourse, not ability.
last_rejected.fix: the technical word, or the word of art
last_rejected.ruling: τεχνικός means 'of art/skill/craft'; 'word of skill' is within normal range. Not a meaning-changing error.

last_rejected.quote: when the human being received the beginning of his generation somewhere far below
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῦ ἀνθρώπου κάτω που λαβόντος τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς γενέσεως
last_rejected.why: "κάτω που" means "down below" spatially/temporally (on earth), not "far below" as degree; "generation" should be "generation" per glossary.
last_rejected.fix: when the human being received the beginning of his generation down below
last_rejected.ruling: κάτω που naturally rendered 'somewhere far below'; spatial/temporal sense preserved. No real error.

last_rejected.why: "αἰῶνες" here means "eternal realms/aeons" or "eternity," not "ages" as time-periods; creatures are beneath the eternal realm.
last_rejected.ruling: αἰών can mean 'age/eternity'; 'lower than the ages' is standard rendering, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: younger than each of the things thought
last_rejected.why: "νεώτερος" means "younger" temporally, but context demands "later than/ posterior to" in order of existence; "each of the things thought" is awkward.
last_rejected.fix: posterior to each of the things conceived
last_rejected.ruling: νεώτερος means 'younger'; temporal posteriority is inherent in 'younger.' Awkwardness is stylistic, not major.

last_rejected.why: Tense: "εἶπεν" is aorist, but context is present gnomic; "he calls him" better captures ongoing force of Scripture's naming.
last_rejected.ruling: εἶπεν aorist commonly rendered 'called' in narrative; 'he calls him' is a preference, not a required fix.

last_rejected.why: "ἐκεῖθεν" means "from that source/from him," not "from there" as place; "dividing off" is weak for ἀπομερίζω (separating/apportioning away).
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκεῖθεν 'from there' can refer to source/person; ἀπομερίζω 'dividing off' is standard. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: "ἀναφέρω" here means "drawn up" (from the spring), not "rises up" spontaneously; passive "is drawn up."
last_rejected.ruling: ἀναφέρω passive 'rises up' fits spring imagery; 'drawn up' is a preference, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: the complete existence of the Son
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν τελείαν ὕπαρξίν σοι τοῦ Υἱοῦ
last_rejected.why: "ὕπαρξις" means "subsistence, existence, reality"; but context emphasizes the Son's complete, perfect being—not just "existence" but "subsistence" or "reality." "Complete existence" is weak.
last_rejected.fix: the perfect subsistence of the Son
last_rejected.ruling: ὕπαρξις 'existence' is standard; 'subsistence/reality' is a preference. 'Complete existence' conveys meaning adequately.
